summary: Both findings were verified at their evidence and both are confirmed, each with a corrected fix. (1, medium) Route 5 does send Conjecture C_n and Corollary 2.2 to AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.6, a layer the accepted RS-07 had already dropped (drop present at the REV-RS-07 commit 61767904, 2026-09-21 17:35 UTC, before the extraction 6e0d73e8 and its review 21adbecc), and the AN packet closes AN.6 with no nodes. So the two items have no live owner. But the red team's destination, SV.5, is rejected. C_n is a statement about short sums of real Dirichlet characters: FIMR §9 ('Direct Estimates for Character Sums') states it as the conjectural extension of Burgess's bound, which gives C_3 with δ = 1/48 (FIMR Corollary 9.1, r = 6). The atlas already has an owner for short character-sum estimates: ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod:ES.0 ('completion of sums; connect to finite-field character-sum producers', input FF.2), whose packet carries the Graham–Ringrose smooth-modulus short-sum estimate routed there by the accepted PAPER-BENNETT-SIKSEK-20. RS-07 distributed AN.6's register to the owner of each unconditional theory (RH/GRH with AN.3, stronger distribution with Bombieri–Vinogradov at SV.3, tuples at SV.4), and that rule puts C_n at ES.0. SV.5 is a sieve stage, and C_n is also consumed outside it: Theorem 3 (item 28) sits at ST.3. The red team missed both points. Its claim that no stage covers short character sums holds for the atlas stage texts only. Authorised fix: retarget route 5 in place to ES.0, rewrite its reason and the notes of items 11 and 12, add one sentence to route 1's reason, and change the matching .md paragraph. (2, low) The extraction has no sourceVersions; what was read is recorded only in source.readSections. Confirmed as presentation, but the red team's second entry, {kind: 'published', … 'not read'}, is rejected: scripts/collation.py provenance() treats any kind 'published' entry as reading the version of record. That already removes PAPER-BHARGAVA-25, PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21 and PAPER-STEVENS-08 from the collation worklist. The fix is one preprint entry whose citation says that the Duke version was not accessible.

sources.citation: Koymans–Milovic, Joint distribution of spins, arXiv 1809.09597v1 (25 September 2018, 23 pp.), the version recorded by the extraction and the red team; hash matches. Read the introduction (pp. 1–3: Theorems 1–3 and their hypotheses C_{|S|n}, C_{tn}, C_n for all n), §2.5 'Short character sums' and §2.6 (pp. 6–7: Conjecture C_n, Corollary 2.2 citing Corollary 7 of [6] = Koymans–Milovic, IMRN, the sieve inputs (2.5)–(2.6)), and §3 up to (3.6) (p. 9, the only use of Corollary 2.2). The version of record, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), no. 8, 1723–1755, doi 10.1215/00127094-2020-0068, was not read, as for the extraction, its review and the red team; neither finding depends on its wording.

Friedlander–Iwaniec–Mazur–Rubin, The spin of prime ideals, arXiv 1110.6331v2 (Invent. Math. 193 (2013) 697–749), the version the extraction consulted. Read the introduction (Theorem 1.1 and the remark that C_3 holds with δ(3) = 1/48 by Burgess), Proposition 6.1, and §9 'Direct Estimates for Character Sums' (PDF p. 39): Burgess's bound (9.2), Corollary 9.1 (r = 6: S_χ(M, N) ≪ N^{5/6} q^{7/144+ε}), the remark that for N about q^{1/n}, n > 3, 'nothing useful is available at present for such short sums (except in the case of special moduli, cf [IK])', and Conjecture C_n (9.4).

findings.reason: Checked at every locator at ff8656a9. None of the files involved has changed since the red team's input revision d4afbc98: the extraction, its review, RS-07.result.json, the AN and ES packets, the SV atlas extract and PAPER-BENNETT-SIKSEK-20. (a) The dead owner. Route 5 of PAPER-KOYMANS-MILOVIC-21.result.json is a source route to AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.6 with items 11 (Conjecture C_n) and 12 (Corollary 2.2). Its reason: 'AN.6 maintains the statement register for conjectural analytic inputs'. The notes of items 11 and 12 say 'Routed to AnalyticNumberTheory AN.6'. RS-07.result.json layers['AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.6'] has action 'drop' ('This is an export/register stage, not a separate mathematical construction'), and the drop is already present at the REV-RS-07 commit 61767904 (#947, 2026-09-21 17:35 UTC), whose report accepts the proposal. The extraction was committed 6e0d73e8 (#1901, 2026-09-22 13:43 UTC) and its review 21adbecc (#2361, 2026-09-23 15:49 UTC). REV-PAPER-KOYMANS-MILOVIC-21.md line 59 reads '5. AN.6: accept. Conjecture C_n and Corollary 2.2 belong in the register of conjectural inputs.' packets/AnalyticNumberTheory--AN.0.json coverage AN.6 is 'closed' with no nodes. So the two items have no live owner. The likely cause is that atlas/roadmaps/AnalyticNumberTheory.json still prints AN.6 with its pre-RS-07 text. RS-07's owners list gives AN.6's contents to AN.2 (zero-free regions), AN.3 (RH/GRH interface), AN.4 (conditional continuation), SV.3 (stronger distribution hypotheses) and SV.4 (prime tuples). None of these is a bound for short character sums, so the finding's core is right, and medium is right: two items would be built nowhere, but no statement is false. (b) The destination: SV.5 is rejected and ES.0 chosen. The paper (p. 6, §2.5 'Short character sums') introduces C_n as 'a conjecture on short character sums appearing in [5]', 'essential for the estimates for sums of type I'. FIMR §9 'Direct Estimates for Character Sums' (arXiv v2, PDF p. 39) states Burgess's bound (9.2) and takes r = 6 to get Corollary 9.1, S_χ(M, N) ≪ N^{5/6} q^{7/144+ε}. With N ≤ Q^{1/3} and q ≤ Q this is Q^{5/18+7/144+ε} = Q^{47/144+ε} = Q^{(1−1/48)/3+ε}, so C_3 holds with δ = 1/48. FIMR then postulate C_n (9.4) because nothing is known for N ≈ q^{1/n}, n > 3, 'except in the case of special moduli, cf [IK]'. C_n is thus the conjectural extension of Burgess's short-sum bound, which is character-sum mathematics, not sieve mathematics. The atlas has an owner for it: ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod:ES.0 'Oscillation and finite sums' ('Develop Weyl differencing, van der Corput, stationary phase and completion of sums; connect to finite-field character-sum producers', input FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums:FF.2; Burgess's method is completion plus the Weil bound). PAPER-BENNETT-SIKSEK-20 routes the Graham–Ringrose short-character-sum estimate at smooth moduli (item 92, the 'special moduli' case FIMR point to) to ES.0, and its review (route 8) accepted that route because ES.0 'already owns' this direction. The ES packet's ES.0 coverage carries those nodes. RS-07 moved each AN.6 register entry to the stage that owns the matching unconditional theory: RH/GRH to AN.3, stronger distribution hypotheses to SV.3 beside Bombieri–Vinogradov, prime tuples to SV.4. By the same rule C_n goes to ES.0. The red team's SV.5 fails on three counts. SV.5 is a sieve stage ('beta/weighted sieves, Chen-type and affine-sieve routes'). C_n is consumed outside SV.5: Theorem 3 (item 28, route 2, ST.3) assumes C_n for all n, which the red team's 'only consumers' sentence omits. And PROTOCOL §15 plans a notion once, with its owner; the next consumers are FIMR itself and Koymans–Milovic IMRN (listed prerequisite; its Corollary 7 is the source of Corollary 2.2), and they would otherwise import a character-sum hypothesis from a sieve application. The red team's 'no stage in the atlas mentions Burgess or short character sums' is true of the atlas stage texts but misses ES.0's packet and the accepted BS20 route. Corollary 2.2 is a pure character-sum consequence of C_n, and I re-derived it. Put d = gcd(q, k) < q (since q ∤ k). χ_d is constant on m ≡ l (mod k), and gcd(q/d, k) = 1 because q is squarefree. So m = l + kt turns the sum into χ_d(l)χ_{q/d}(k) times a sum of the non-principal real character χ_{q/d}(t + l·k̄) over an interval of at most N ≤ q^{1/n} integers. C_n with Q = q ≥ 3 then gives C(n, ε)q^{(1−δ)/n+ε}, the E2-corrected form. Adding no Burgess item is right: the paper never uses Burgess, as the red team says. The absence of Pólya–Vinogradov and Burgess from both pinned libraries was checked in the baseline declarations index, so items 11 and 12 stay 'missing'. Authorised fix, in research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-KOYMANS-MILOVIC-21.result.json and the matching paragraph of PAPER-KOYMANS-MILOVIC-21.md only. (1) Keep route 5 at position 5, because make_queue.accepted_routes matches routes to the review's verdicts by position. Change its roadmap to 'ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod' and its stages to ['ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod:ES.0'], keep items 11 and 12, and replace the reason with: 'ES.0 owns estimates for short character sums: completion of sums fed by the finite-field bounds of FF.2, and the Graham–Ringrose smooth-modulus estimate routed here by PAPER-BENNETT-SIKSEK-20. FIMR's Conjecture C_n (FIMR §9, (9.4)) is the conjectural extension of Burgess's bound to intervals of length Q^{1/n}; Burgess with r = 6 gives C_3 with δ = 1/48 (FIMR Corollary 9.1), and nothing is known for n ≥ 4 at general moduli. ES.0 states C_n as a named hypothesis, never as a theorem, and derives Corollary 2.2 from it. Its consumers carry it in their statements: the type I estimate and Theorems 1–2 at SV.5 (items 14, 23, 24) and Theorem 3 at ST.3 (item 28). This follows RS-07, which dropped AN.6 and moved each conjectural input to the owner of the matching unconditional theory.' (2) Item 11's note becomes: 'A conjecture beyond Burgess, which gives C_3 with δ = 1/48 (FIMR Corollary 9.1, r = 6); no case n ≥ 4 is known. Stated at ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod ES.0 as a named hypothesis, not a theorem; items 14, 23, 24 and 28 assume it.' Item 12's note becomes: 'Statement with the +ε restored (E2). Derived from item 11 at ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod ES.0: with d = gcd(q, k) < q, χ_d is constant on the progression and gcd(q/d, k) = 1, so the sum is a short sum of the non-principal character χ_{q/d}, bounded by C_n with Q = q.' Statements, kinds, statuses and locators are unchanged. (3) Route 1's reason gains the sentence: 'Conjecture C_{|S|n} (C_{tn}) and Corollary 2.2 enter items 14, 23 and 24 as explicit hypotheses imported from ES.0 (route 5).' Items 11 and 12 are not added to route 1. (4) In the .md, the route-5 paragraph ('5. Source of AnalyticNumberTheory AN.6 …') becomes 'Source of ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod ES.0 (2 items)', with the reason in (1) in one or two sentences. Re-run check_paper.py. Out of scope: REV-PAPER-KOYMANS-MILOVIC-21.md and PAPER-KOYMANS-MILOVIC-21.review.json are not edited, and this verdict supersedes the review's route-5 reason. The summary does not mention AN.6 and stays. Maintainer notes, not fixer edits: atlas/roadmaps/AnalyticNumberTheory.json still shows AN.6 with its pre-RS-07 text, so extractions keep choosing it. PAPER-CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20 (GRH for Rankin–Selberg, whose RS-07 owner is AN.3) and PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-16 (Schinzel's Hypothesis H and HH1) also still route to AN.6.

Checked at ff8656a9. PAPER-KOYMANS-MILOVIC-21.result.json has eight sourceIssues (E1–E8, all 'affects': 'nothing') and no sourceVersions key. What was read is recorded only in the free text of source.readSections: arXiv v1, read 2026-09-22, SHA-256 d56a738a…f433, and 'The Duke version (2021, 33 printed pages) was not accessible'. I downloaded arXiv v1 on 2026-09-30 and the hash matches. PROTOCOL §18 says the file 'records what was read, alongside sourceIssues', in the sourceVersions format. scripts/check_errata.py versions_checked requires the list only when a finding quotes a stated result, so the file passes. The substance is present, so this is presentation, and low is right. Low findings do not make a fix job by themselves, but FIX-RT-PAPER-KOYMANS-MILOVIC-21 exists for finding 1 and should apply this too. The gap is systemic: 191 of the 229 extractions with sourceIssues have no sourceVersions. It has no machine effect here: scripts/collation.py falls back to the searched notes and classifies this paper as 'preprint', and it has no stated-result findings. Correction to the red team's fix: its second entry, {'kind': 'published', 'citation': 'Duke … not openly accessible, not read', …}, is rejected. collation.provenance() returns 'published' whenever any sourceVersions entry has kind 'published', without reading the citation. Such an entry would therefore declare the version of record read, and would drop the paper from the collation worklist as soon as a finding quotes a stated result. A read-only run of collation.records() shows this already happens to PAPER-BHARGAVA-25 (7 stated-result findings), PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21 (4) and PAPER-STEVENS-08 (4), all of which carry a 'published … not read' entry. Authorised fix, in PAPER-KOYMANS-MILOVIC-21.result.json only: add top-level 'sourceVersions': [{'kind': 'preprint', 'url': 'https://arxiv.org/pdf/1809.09597v1', 'read': '2026-09-22', 'sha256': 'd56a738ae1b1487dd01b92b7084dd6bd4b9a041a85efdd2fac66b86afd8af433', 'citation': 'arXiv 1809.09597v1 (25 September 2018), read completely; the version of record, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), no. 8, 1723–1755, doi 10.1215/00127094-2020-0068, was not accessible, so locators and source issues are scoped to arXiv v1.'}], as in PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26. source.readSections stays. Re-run check_paper.py. Maintainer note, not a fixer edit: collation.provenance() should not count a kind 'published' entry that says it was not read, or the convention should forbid such entries.
